summary: Full-extraction pass over 14 stored Canadian documents: the CRA Offshore Tax Informant Program pages and privacy impact assessment, eight OSC award news releases, and three OSC Whistleblower Program pages. Most numbers were already in the data; added the 2016-2022 update's tip breakdowns (channel, misconduct type, subject, geography, internal reporting), hotline calls, respondents, missing rules, and three events.

ledger.contains: CRA web page 'Report offshore tax cheating - Outcomes' (modified 2026-08-11): reward of 5-15% of federal tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) if at least $100,000 is collected; levels 5/7.5/10/12.5/15%; no upfront payments, partial payments possible after the threshold, payment only after objection and appeal rights expire; rewards taxable; grounds for ineligibility or contract termination; grievance panel; factor table (quality, relevance, cooperation, value). No statistics. The 5%, 15% and $100,000 rules were already recorded; this pass adds the discretionary rule (reward level set by the CRA from listed factors).

CRA web page 'Report offshore tax cheating - Overview' (modified 2026-08-11): what OTIP is (rewards for information on major international tax evasion leading to collection), examples of reportable situations, confidentiality of informant and taxpayer. No numbers, no reward rules, no dates; used only as context (shows the programme still open).

CRA Privacy Impact Assessment summary 'Offshore Tax Informant Program v 3.0' (2024-11-12): legal authority (ITA s. 220(1), ETA s. 275(1)); programme description and reward rules (5-15% of additional federal tax assessed and collected; at least $100,000 collected); eligibility exclusions (incl. anonymous informants, CRA and government employees); identity checks; what's new (procedure updates, workload management system 2022, new system planned 2025); scope; privacy risk ratings (levels 1-4) and handling of Protected B/C information; OTIP described as permanent with no sunset date. No statistics on tips, contracts, rewards or taxes. Out of scope: privacy risk ratings, TBS registration and bank numbers. Extracted: 4 rules and 2 context events.

OSC news release 27 Feb 2019: first awards by a Canadian securities regulator, CAD 7,499,000 to three whistleblowers on separate matters; quotes from the Chair and the Director of Enforcement; confidentiality. Already in the data as a case (c-8d4482243d) and an event (e-862d2caaf4); no other numbers (no cumulative total, no sanctions amount). Nothing added.

OSC news release 6 Apr 2020: CAD 525,000 award to a company outsider; cumulative 'more than $8 million' awarded since July 2016; restates the up to $5 million award cap. Award (case c-3806e64152) and cumulative (o-4d6304a470) already recorded; the cap is boilerplate already recorded as a rule from the programme pages, not repeated as a rule row. Nothing added.

OSC news release 17 Nov 2020: CAD 585,000 in total to three whistleblowers (company outsiders with technical analysis); cumulative 'more than $8.6 million'; restates the up to $5 million cap. Case c-999bcb7707 and cumulative o-b6770ca57a already recorded; cap is boilerplate (recorded from programme pages). Nothing added.

OSC news release 1 Mar 2022: $240,000 award to joint whistleblowers, tip from outside Canada; cumulative 'nearly $9 million'; restates the up to $5 million cap. Case c-eba8a023a1 and cumulative o-a825fb5629 already recorded; cap is boilerplate (recorded from programme pages). Nothing added.

OSC news release 20 Mar 2023: award of approximately $481,000 to an insider; cumulative $9.33 million awarded; tips have led to enforcement action against 19 respondents and approximately $48 million in monetary sanctions and voluntary payments; tips come in anonymously through counsel and from across Canada, the U.S. and abroad; up to $5 million cap; the OSC published its programme update on 9 March 2023. Already recorded: case c-af3cd21ca2, cumulative o-a3d82a11f1, sanctions o-d53cba0ae9. Added: 19 respondents (proposed indicator respondents_sanctioned) and the 9 March 2023 publication event. Cap and anonymous filing through counsel are boilerplate already recorded as rules from the programme pages.

OSC news release 27 Feb 2024: CAD 1,500,000 award to an insider; cumulative 'more than $10 million'; up to $5 million cap; appeal for tips on greenwashing, audit firms, algorithms and AI. Case c-aa2ac08c78 and cumulative o-c2ee7de8b7 already recorded; cap is boilerplate (recorded from programme pages). Nothing added.

OSC news release 15 May 2024: $300,000 award to a senior whistleblower whose information led a firm to rectify a compliance issue; cumulative 'more than $10 million'; up to $5 million cap. Case c-1ba7593e69 and cumulative o-0b34d51680 already recorded; cap is boilerplate. Nothing added.

OSC news release 23 Oct 2024: award of nearly $150,000 to an international whistleblower (not an employee) about an early-stage firm; cumulative 'more than $10 million'; up to $5 million cap; protections. Case c-087c769eba and cumulative o-b591d82918 already recorded; cap is boilerplate. Nothing added.

OSC web page 'Award eligibility and process' (2026): Policy 15-601 award criteria (over $1 million in sanctions and/or voluntary payments), voluntary and original information, ineligible information, 120-day window after internal reporting, individual eligibility (compliance/audit roles generally excluded), culpable, anonymous (through lawyers) and joint whistleblowers, timelines (paid after appeals expire), award amount 5-15% up to $5 million ($1.5M not contingent on collections, $1.5-5M contingent), discretion and factors, confidentiality, tax. No statistics. Five rules were already recorded from this page; added award cap $5M, non-contingent cap $1.5M and the $1M threshold.

OSC Whistleblower Program landing page (2026): launched July 2016, first of its kind by a Canadian securities regulator; reward up to $5 million; examples of violations; featured news item on the 27 Feb 2024 CAD 1,500,000 award (not updated for the May and Oct 2024 awards); quote from the Coinsquare settlement reasons; protections (confidentiality, anonymous reporting, anti-reprisal); Office of the Whistleblower and hotline. Launch (event e-70baa8b6a6) and the Feb 2024 award (case c-aa2ac08c78) already recorded from other sources. Added: award cap and anonymous-reporting rules.

OSC web page 'Update on the OSC Whistleblower Program 2016 to 2022' (data to 31 Mar 2022; published 9 Mar 2023 per the 20 Mar 2023 news release): Office of the Whistleblower (626 hotline calls; outreach to ~7,000 individuals through 100+ presentations); awards ($9.33 million to 11 whistleblowers; ~$48 million in sanctions and voluntary payments against 19 respondents; recipients' profiles in words only); how awards are determined (5-15%, $1M threshold, $5M cap, $1.5M not contingent on collections, CEO discretion, appeals must expire); tips (797 tips from 840+ whistleblowers, 93% online; 17% average annual growth, +89% FY2022 vs FY2018; misconduct-type pie chart; 50%/33% of securities tips naming public companies/registrants; geography 63% Ontario, 17% rest of Canada, 15% US/Australia/UK/China, 30 countries; internal reporting 63% and 84%); protections; looking ahead (planned policy amendments). Images: highlights, award process, tips bar chart, misconduct pie chart, world map; numbers taken from alt text where printed. Already recorded: awards, individuals, sanctions, tips total, cap and threshold rules, launch and look-ahead events. Added 19 observations and 5 rules.
